verses.text: These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, and Shelah; which three were born to him of Shua’s daughter the Canaanitess. Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in Yahweh’s  sight; and he killed him.
Tamar his daughter-in-law bore him Perez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah were five.
The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara; five of them in all.
The son of Carmi: Achar, the troubler of Israel, who committed a trespass in the devoted thing.
The son of Ethan: Azariah.
The sons also of Hezron, who were born to him: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
Ram became the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah;
and Nahshon became the father of Salma, and Salma became the father of Boaz,
and Boaz became the father of Obed, and Obed became the father of Jesse;
and Jesse became the father of his firstborn Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimea the third,
Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Ozem the sixth, David the seventh;
and their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, three.
Abigail bore Amasa; and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Caleb the son of Hezron became the father of children of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth; and these were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
Azubah died, and Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur.
Hur became the father of Uri, and Uri became the father of Bezalel.
Afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he took as wife when he was sixty years old; and she bore him Segub.
Segub became the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
Geshur and Aram took the towns of Jair from them, with Kenath, and its villages, even sixty cities. All these were the sons of Machir the father of Gilead.
After Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, Abijah Hezron’s wife bore him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron were Ram the firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel had another wife, whose name was Atarah. She was the mother of Onam.
The sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.
The name of the wife of Abishur was Abihail; and she bore him Ahban and Molid.
The sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim; but Seled died without children.
The son of Appaim: Ishi. The son of Ishi: Sheshan. The son of Sheshan: Ahlai.
The sons of Jada the brother of Shammai: Jether and Jonathan; and Jether died without children.
The sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel.
Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant as wife; and she bore him Attai.
Attai became the father of Nathan, and Nathan became the father of Zabad,
and Zabad became the father of Ephlal, and Ephlal became the father of Obed,
and Obed became the father of Jehu, and Jehu became the father of Azariah,
and Azariah became the father of Helez, and Helez became the father of Eleasah,
and Eleasah became the father of Sismai, and Sismai became the father of Shallum,
and Shallum became the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah became the father of Elishama.
The sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel were Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph; and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron.
The sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema became the father of Raham, the father of Jorkeam; and Rekem became the father of Shammai.
The son of Shammai was Maon; and Maon was the father of Beth Zur.
Ephah, Caleb’s concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez; and Haran became the father of Gazez.
The sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Maacah, Caleb’s concubine, bore Sheber and Tirhanah.
She bore also Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbena, and the father of Gibea; and the daughter of Caleb was Achsah.
These were the sons of Caleb, the son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim,
Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth Gader.
Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim had sons: Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth.
The families of Kiriath Jearim: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites; from them came the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.
The sons of Salma: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth Beth Joab, and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites.
The families of scribes who lived at Jabez: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These are the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.

footnotes.content: The chronicler names the twelve sons of Israel—not by their own strength, but as the Lord's chosen family. Notice how he keeps the lineage in order, showing us that genealogies matter in God's kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this genealogy: the Lord does not forget. In a world where names are lost and stories are erased, this chapter proclaims that God remembers every life, every covenant-keeper, every child of His promise. We, too, are written in His book.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six more sons complete the list—and in them are all the tribes that will carry God's covenant into the future. Each name represents a family that God will work through in ways they never imagined.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here we see Judah's sons through a Canaanite woman, yet the record does not shy from the judgment: Er was wicked, and the Lord took him. Even in the chosen line, God's justice is swift and true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tamar, a daughter-in-law who had to demand justice, bore the sons that carried the Davidic line. Sometimes the Lord works through a woman's quiet courage when men look away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Perez—whose name means "breaking through"—came Hezron and Hamul. The Lord often chooses names that point to His purposes: even a breach can become a blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zerah's line included men of renown—Ethan, Heman—whose names appear in the Psalms as wise men and singers. In God's house, musicians and thinkers have their place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Achar earned the name "troubler of Israel"—his theft of devoted things brought judgment on all his people. One person's betrayal of covenant can reach far beyond their own life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A single son, Azariah, carries forward the line of Ethan. Sometimes the narrowest branch proves crucial to God's design.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Hezron came three sons: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai. The Lord divides inheritances so that multiple branches bear witness to His care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Through Ram came Amminadab, Nahshon (a prince), Salma, Boaz, and Obed. In this line walks Boaz—a man of honor who loved a foreigner with covenant kindness. These are links in the chain that leads to David, and through David to the King of kings.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jesse was the father of seven sons, but the seventh one—David—was the least valued. The Lord often chooses the overlooked one, the one tending sheep while others gathered at the feast. From the youngest, the anointed king came.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David's sisters, Zeruiah and Abigail, mothered men of war and wisdom. In God's economy, a woman's strength often shapes the strength of her sons—and the chronicler records her name with honor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Caleb married twice: first Azubah, then Ephrath. His life spans generations and journeys; he knew the Lord's faithfulness across decades. After loss, he loved again—a quiet picture of resilience in God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Hur came Uri, and from Uri came Bezalel—the master craftsman who built the Tabernacle. God's artisans carry His vision just as prophets do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hezron took a wife at sixty years old and became a father still. The Lord's mercies are new each morning; age does not close the door to new chapters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jair possessed twenty-three cities in Gilead. The inheritance of names and lands reminds us that God's promises extend through generations, each one building on what the Lord gave their fathers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Territories shift between hands; Geshur and Aram reclaimed towns Jair had held. Nothing we hold is truly ours to keep—the Lord gives and takes according to His will.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After Hezron died, his widow bore a son—Ashhur. Even in death, a man's name continues through those left behind, and the Lord sustains the family through sorrow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerahmeel, the firstborn, received five sons—Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah. The firstborn's inheritance was often the heaviest; bearing a great name carried great responsibility.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerahmeel took another wife, Atarah, and she became mother to Onam. A second marriage can bring new blessings; the Lord does not measure love by the first chapter only.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Ram—Maaz, Jamin, and Eker—appear only in genealogy, yet the chronicler records their names. Every person who walked with the Lord is remembered in His sight, known or unknown to the world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Onam fathered Shammai, who fathered Nadab and Abishur. The chronicler is careful to trace these lines—not to glorify them, but to show that God remembers the seed of covenant keepers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abihail bore Abishur's sons—Ahban and Molid. A wife's name and children are recorded here as part of the covenant line. Women are not incidental in God's record of His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seled died without children, yet his brother Appaim continued the line. When one branch ends, another grows—God's covenant is not fragile; it endures.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Through Ishi, Sheshan, and Ahlai, the line continued unbroken. Simple names, quiet lives—yet they carried forward the promise their ancestors knew.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jether died childless, but his brother Jonathan's sons—Peleth and Zaza—kept the family living. The Lord raises up others when one generation cannot bear children.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Jonathan are counted among the sons of Jerahmeel. In God's family, lineage is not erased; every name belongs to the whole people, and the whole people belongs to God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sheshan had no sons, only daughters—and so he gave his daughter to his Egyptian servant Jarha. Sometimes the Lord breaks convention to fulfill His design; a servant became family through an act of trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The long chain continues—Attai, Nathan, Zabad, and onward through Jekamiah to Elishama. Each generation heard the promise from the one before, carrying it forward like a lamp passed from hand to hand. The Lord's covenant transcends any earthly boundary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel had sons who fathered towns—Mesha and Mareshah founded Ziph and Hebron. A man's name and his works often live on in the land itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Hebron—Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema—each carried a father's hope into their own generation. The strength of one man's faith ripples through his children.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shema fathered Raham, Rekem fathered Shammai. The chronicler traces not just straight lines but the branching tree—showing how God's people spread and multiply across the land.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shammai became father of Maon, who founded Beth Zur. In biblical genealogy, a man and his city often become one—he builds a place, and his name lives there forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore three sons: Haran, Moza, and Gazez. In a household, all are counted—the chronicler's pen did not favor one wife's children over another's.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jahdai's sons—Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph—are named, though we know nothing more of them. The Lord knows each one; fame does not measure a person's worth in His eyes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Maacah, another of Caleb's concubines, bore Sheber and Tirhanah. A man's lineage grew through many women; in this, we see both human fragility and God's faithfulness to bless despite it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Maacah bore three more sons and a daughter—Achsah. In this genealogy, the daughter's name is preserved as carefully as any son's. Women's names matter in God's record.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Caleb, son of Hur, fathered Shobal—and Shobal's name means "flowing"—founder of Kiriath Jearim. In genealogy, a name often hints at character or calling; the Lord gives names that fit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Salma fathered Bethlehem—the very city where the Line of Judah would culminate in a Savior's birth. A founder's name became inseparable from his city; generations later, that city bore witness to Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shobal's son Haroeh lived in the Menuhoth, a place name meaning "rest." Even in genealogy's dry branches, we catch hints of the peace God gives to those who trust Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The families that came from Kiriath Jearim—Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, Mishraites—multiplied and spread. From one ancestor, many clans arose, each carrying the covenant seed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Salma included Bethlehem and the Netophathites. These places and people, recorded here in a genealogy, became centers where God's word dwelt and witnesses lived.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The families of scribes at Jabez—the Tirathites, Shimeathites, Sucathites—were Kenites descended from Hammath. Scribes kept records, preserved words, wrote God's law; their labor was sacred work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
